headers.//: Site-wide: revalidate on every request so a new deploy is picked up on the next normal reload, with no hard-refresh and no stale service worker. This previously also sent `no-store`; that is dropped because it forbids storing a copy at all while buying nothing extra. MEASURED on this host: Firebase Hosting never returns 304 -- it answers 200 with a full body for both If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since, retested with exact br etags -- so revalidation always costs a full download here and only a real max-age can avoid one. The Quran edition JSONs used to carry such a max-age rule; they are no longer served from Hosting at all (they come from GitHub via jsDelivr, see web_edition_json.dart), so that rule was removed rather than left as dead config. If you ever DO add a path-specific rule: Firebase applies header rules LAST-MATCH-WINS, verified by deploying both orders, so it must come AFTER this `**` entry to take effect.
